w: Bhagwatcharan Swami came from Vidyanagar for darshan. The sadhus asked him, "Why didn't you come here on the day of Shastriji Maharaj's shraddh (death anniversary)?"

Bhagwatcharan Swami said, "That day I was in Mahelav." Then, joking, he said, "I always hold on to the root. Because Shastriji Maharaj was born in Mahelav, today there is this Sarangpur and everything else. The root is the root." He looked towards Pramukh Swami Maharaj for support, and Swamishri immediately said, "We never make distinctions of greater and lesser in this way. Whether it is the birthplace, the place of work or the place of samadhi, all are the same. If we try to make them greater and lesser, it would be an offence. One cannot say Chhapaiya is greater and Gadhada lesser. Everything that came into connection with Him is equally divine." Even in jest, Swamishri did not support any distinction in divinity.

When one realises the glory of God one will not be attracted or impressed by worldly pleasures. For us, having met God and His holy Sadhu is of highest importance.
It is because of spiritual discourses (katha) that one is infused with enthusiasm, strength and confidence.
Worldly praise and honor is not important but abiding by agna (moral instruction) and Upasana (creed) is a measure of greatness.

Through the inspiration of Swamishri a three-shikhar mandir in pink stone is under construction in 'Akshar Vadi'. The mandir will become a centre of BAPS socio-spiritual activities for the uplift of society. The mandir complex will include a polyclinic, a residential school from standards 1 to 12, a hostel for college students, an exhibition on Indian culture and offices for children, youth and women's activities. Today, the mahapuja ritual for the placing of the first carved pillar in the mandir construction project had begun. Swamishri performed puja, arti and mantra pushpanjali of the pillar-base and the ornate pillar. After blessing the assembly, the pillar was placed on top of the kumbhi (pillar-base) by Swamishri.

Patotsav and Kirtan Aradhana In the morning, a traditional mahapuja ceremony was held in the mandir to celebrate the patostsav of Kampala mandir. Swamishi’s ill health prevented him from attending, but Viveksagar Swami presided over the mahapuja ceremony on his behalf. In the evening, Swamishri arrived in the mandir for the patotsav assembly.
Due to ill health, Swamishri was unable to visit Jinja. However, he instructed Doctor Swami and 30 sadhus and parshads to go on his behalf for the Jinja Mandir murti-pratishtha.
From early morning, the traditional Vedic murti-pratishtha rituals were performed in the presence of Doctor Swami.

Afterwards, in the assembly, the balaks performed a traditional welcome dance. After speeches by senior devotees and local dignitaries, Doctor Swami addressed the assembly. Thus, with Swamishri’s blessings the 2-day Jinja Mandir Murti-Pratishtha Mahotsav was celebrated in grand style.
After darshan of Thakorji, Swamishri blessed 16 youths of Bodala who had cycled 1001 km to New Delhi to serve in the inauguration of Swaminarayan Akshardham.
In the morning, Swamishri visited the main monument and during his detailed inspection of the work, gave necessary guidance on several important aspects.
In the evening a special assembly was held for the 1500 volunteers who were currently present helping in the preparations for the inauguration festival.

st.t: BAPS News – National Karyakar Shibir – Sunday 30 September 2007
w: This year’s National Karyakar Shibir, entitled ‘Adarsh’ was held in the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj on Sunday 30 September 2007 at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London. Over 800 delegates representing 33 centres from UK & Europe attended the event, where Bal, Kishore, Yuvak and Sanyukta Mandals explained the components of the title (‘Antardrashti’, ‘Dradhta’, ‘Adar’, ‘Ruchi’, ‘Samjan’ and ‘Het’) through a variety of media throughout the day.

Ishwarcharan Swami introduced the purpose of the Shibir, emphasising the fortune of the gathered karyakars for the opportunity of seva. The principles of ‘Antardrashti’ were explained by Ishwarcharan Swami and elaborated further with a question-answer session with senior sadhus. The second session revolved around the importance of ‘Dradhta’ in niyams with a narrative from Anandswarup Swami and references from Swamishri through a video presentation.

‘Adar’ was the third component of the Shibir where Satsang progression and in particular, the subject of respect was addressed. The importance of ‘Ruchi’ was explained by Atmatrupt Swami, and further demonstrated with an enlightening sketch. The following session presented the topic of ‘Samjan’ including an informative debate and a question-answer session about mahima.

The evening finale was focussed on ‘Het’ where touching episodes from the life of Swamishri were narrated by Narayancharan Swami. An entertaining series of short sketches provided an informative summary of the day with each theme of ‘Adarsh’ enacted with appropriate scenes.

The conclusion was fittingly provided by Swamishri who explained the qualities of an ideal karyakar, commenting in particular on the importance of mahima and observing virtues in others. Swamishri also encouraged everyone to introspect on what they had learnt in the Shibir. Following the conclusion of the Shibir, the joyous mood continued as devotees proceeded for samip darshan of Swamishri.

Today, when Mahant Swami Maharaj came to his room, his attendants recalled an incident: when Swamishri came to this residence, he saw that there was no photo of Pramukh Swami Maharaj anywhere here, because this residence had been Pramukh Swami Maharaj's. He would never let his own photo be put up. So as soon as he arrived, Swamishri said, "Put up a photo of Swamibapa here."
Swamishri's instruction was carried out immediately, and two beautiful photos were put up here.
Today the sadhus asked, "Swami! What games did you play at school?"
Swamishri said, "Football, boxing, cricket, hockey..."
Hearing so much, the sadhus' amazement knew no bounds. And they asked in between, "Swami! You played so much?"
Swamishri said, "At our school all games were compulsory." Then he said, "In winter we played cricket. In the rainy season, football. And in summer we played hockey."
The sadhus asked, "Were you a bowler or a batsman in cricket?"
Swamishri laughed and said, "A bit of this and that." That is, he was not especially skilled in any area.
The sadhus accepted this and were about to ask further, but Swamishri said slowly, "Everyone got out to my bowling. I bowled grasscutter balls."
The sadhus were greatly amazed. Even good bowlers stumble when bowling a grasscutter, that is, a yorker.
Explaining the speciality of that ball, Swamishri said, "Even if I bowled it like this (from high up), it would not bounce. It went along the ground."
Swamishri was asked, "In football, which position did you play?"
Swamishri said, "Left full back."
The sadhus asked, "Swami! Are you a left hander when playing?"
Swamishri said, "No."
"Then why did you choose the left full back position?"

A left footed player plays well at left full back, so mostly left footed players play in this position; that is why the sadhus had asked this question. So Swamishri was asked, "If you were not left footed, why did you play at left full back?"

Swamishri smiled meaningfully and said, "In our team no one else was comfortable there, so I played there." Then he said slowly, "Samp and suhradbhav (unity and friendliness) from the very beginning!"
Then Swamishri spoke of another game: "At our school the 'three legged race' was played."

In this game, one's own leg and one leg of the other player are tied together. So there is our one leg, one leg made of the two tied together, and the other player's one leg: together the two players have three legs. And the race is run like this.
Swamishri said, "In that too, I put my left leg so that it would suit the other person. And even so we came first!"
The sadhus were immersed in wonder and admiration.
These two incidents of Swamishri are enough to explain that we must maintain unity from our own side, thinking, "What can I do for unity?", and act accordingly.

ds.t: A left hand drive golf cart
w: Mahant Swami Maharaj came to the golf cart to go to the Bal Din (Children's Day). Pausing for a moment, he asked the sadhus with curiosity, "Is this golf cart made here?"
The sadhus said "Yes."
But Swamishri immediately explained why the question had arisen in his mind: "This is left hand drive."
The sadhus said, "Oh...!"
Because in England vehicles are right hand drive. No one had noticed this. But how much Swamishri's keen eye notices!
The sadhus said, "Swami! We will find out and let you know."

Tonight a phone call came from a Jewish doctor. He had had the privilege of examining Mahant Swami Maharaj. When the conversation was over, Swamishri said to him, "Shalom!" It is a word used in the Jewish language, just as we say "Jai Swaminarayan".
More than three months had passed since meeting this doctor, but Swamishri had remembered it. How many such little things Swamishri remembers!
